subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Buying Time
description: Learn Buying Time in one minute.

hook.text: Hiring someone to clean your house for $80 buys you three hours. People who buy time report greater life satisfaction.

buildup.text: Whillans' research found that using money to eliminate unpleasant tasks increases happiness more than buying luxury.

discovery.text: Time poverty — feeling like you never have enough time — is a stronger predictor of unhappiness than income poverty.

twist.text: But people methodically choose material purchases over time-saving ones, even when they can afford both.

climax.text: Before your next purchase, ask: would I be happier spending this money to buy back my time instead?

punchline.text: The best thing money can buy is time.

quiz.question: What did research find about buying time?
options: It has no effect on happiness
Using money to eliminate unpleasant tasks increases happiness
Only wealthy people benefit from buying time
